note: Which parameters actually matter on Live's stock devices, and what they do musically. Keyed by the `class_name` that get_device_parameters reports, so the two join up. Parameter indices are deliberately absent, they shift between device versions, so match by name. This covers the devices most used in practice, not every device Live ships.
reading_values: Almost every Live parameter is 0.0-1.0 regardless of what it displays; `display_value` from get_device_parameters is the only reliable way to know what a number means. Quantized parameters (filter types, sync rates, modes) report `value_items` and their value is an index into that list.

devices.name: Auto Filter
devices.summary: The filter for sweeps and movement. The workhorse for build-ups, drops and taking the top off a pad.

key_parameters.name: Frequency
key_parameters.does: Cutoff. The parameter you automate for a sweep. Around 0.25 is muffled, 0.6 is open, 0.9+ is barely filtering.

key_parameters.name: Resonance
key_parameters.does: Emphasis at the cutoff. A little adds character; past ~0.7 it whistles and can dominate.

key_parameters.name: Filter Type
key_parameters.does: Low-pass removes treble (the usual choice), high-pass removes bass (good for thinning a pad under a vocal), band-pass narrows to a band, Notch scoops a band out.

key_parameters.name: Filter Slope
key_parameters.does: 12 dB is gentle, 24 dB is decisive. Use 24 for dramatic sweeps.

key_parameters.name: Filter Morph
key_parameters.does: Only does anything in Morph or DJ filter modes; inert otherwise.

key_parameters.name: LFO Amount
key_parameters.does: Wobble depth. With Frequency it gives auto-wah movement without automation.

key_parameters.name: LFO Frequency
key_parameters.does: Wobble rate. Sync it to the tempo for rhythmic filtering.

devices.gotchas: Frequency is not linear in hertz: the same numeric step moves far more at the top than the bottom. Read display_value when you care about the actual frequency.

devices.name: Roar
devices.summary: Saturation and distortion, from gentle warmth to destruction. Live 12's most capable colour device.

key_parameters.name: Amount
key_parameters.does: Drive. The main control. Everything else shapes what this does. Low values thicken, high values distort.

key_parameters.name: Output Gain
key_parameters.does: Compensates for the level Amount adds. Raise Amount and this usually needs lowering.

key_parameters.name: Tone
key_parameters.does: Tilts the saturation brighter or darker. Darker suits bass, brighter suits pads that need presence.

key_parameters.name: Feedback
key_parameters.does: Feeds output back in. Adds resonant grit; unstable at high settings.

key_parameters.name: Dry/Wet
key_parameters.does: Blend. On a pad, keeping some dry preserves the original body.

key_parameters.name: Filter Frequency
key_parameters.does: Shapes what gets saturated: filter before driving to keep low end clean.

devices.gotchas: Saturation adds harmonics upward, so a driven pad occupies more high-frequency space than its notes suggest. Expect it to crowd anything above it.

devices.name: Echo
devices.summary: Delay with character. Best on a return track so several parts can share it.

key_parameters.name: L Time
key_parameters.does: Left delay time. Synced to tempo by default. 1/8 and 1/4 are the safe musical choices; dotted 1/8 gives the familiar trailing feel.

key_parameters.name: R Time
key_parameters.does: Right delay time. Setting it different from L widens the image.

key_parameters.name: Feedback
key_parameters.does: How many repeats. Past ~0.7 the tail barely dies; at 1.0 it self-oscillates.

key_parameters.name: Dry/Wet
key_parameters.does: On a return track set this to 1.0 and control the amount with the track's send instead.

key_parameters.name: Input Gain
key_parameters.does: Drives the delay line without changing the send level.

key_parameters.name: Reverb Level
key_parameters.does: Built-in reverb on the repeats. Blurs the tail into something more ambient.

devices.gotchas: Feedback plus Reverb Level accumulates energy, a patch that sounds fine on one note can wash out under a chord.

devices.name: Reverb
devices.summary: Space and depth. Almost always better on a return track than as an insert.

key_parameters.name: Decay Time
key_parameters.does: How long the tail lasts. Short reads as a room, long as a wash. Long decays on a pad quickly become the loudest thing in the mix.

key_parameters.name: Dry/Wet
key_parameters.does: 1.0 on a return track; control the amount with each track's send.

key_parameters.name: Predelay
key_parameters.does: Gap before the reverb starts. A little keeps the source distinct rather than smeared.

key_parameters.name: Room Size
key_parameters.does: Character of the space, independent of decay length.

key_parameters.name: Lo Cut
key_parameters.does: Removes bass from the reverb. Almost always worth engaging, reverberated low end is what makes a mix muddy.

key_parameters.name: Hi Cut
key_parameters.does: Removes treble from the tail, pushing the space further back.

devices.gotchas: Reverb on a low-register part is the most common cause of a congested mix. Filter the bass out of the send, or do not send bass at all.

devices.name: Compressor
devices.summary: Level control. Used for consistency, or deliberately for pumping.

key_parameters.name: Threshold
key_parameters.does: Level above which it acts. Lower means more compression.

key_parameters.name: Ratio
key_parameters.does: How firmly. 2:1-4:1 is gentle control, 8:1 and above is limiting.

key_parameters.name: Attack
key_parameters.does: How fast it clamps. Fast tames transients; slow lets them through, which keeps a part punchy.

key_parameters.name: Release
key_parameters.does: How fast it lets go. Too fast pumps audibly; sync it to the tempo when you want that.

key_parameters.name: Makeup
key_parameters.does: Restores the level compression removed.

key_parameters.name: Dry/Wet
key_parameters.does: Parallel compression: keeps the original dynamics while adding a controlled layer underneath.

devices.gotchas: Compressing a pad reduces the movement that makes it interesting. If it needs level control, consider automating volume instead.

devices.name: EQ Eight
devices.summary: Surgical frequency shaping. The right tool when two parts fight for the same register.

key_parameters.name: 1 Frequency A
key_parameters.does: Band 1 centre. Bands are numbered 1-8, each with Frequency, Gain, Q and a filter type.

key_parameters.name: 1 Gain A
key_parameters.does: Cut or boost. Cutting is usually more transparent than boosting.

key_parameters.name: 1 Resonance A
key_parameters.does: Q, bandwidth. Narrow for removing a specific problem, wide for tonal shaping.

key_parameters.name: 1 Filter Type A
key_parameters.does: High-pass, low-shelf, bell, notch, high-shelf, low-pass.

devices.gotchas: Parameter names carry a band number and an A/B channel suffix, so always read them from get_device_parameters rather than guessing. A high-pass on everything that is not bass is the single most effective mix move.

devices.name: Operator
devices.summary: FM synthesis. Excellent for bells, metallic timbres, electric-piano tones and hard basses.

key_parameters.name: Osc-A Coarse
key_parameters.does: Carrier pitch ratio. Integer ratios sound harmonic; non-integer sound metallic or bell-like.

key_parameters.name: Osc-B Coarse
key_parameters.does: Modulator ratio, the main determinant of timbre in FM.

key_parameters.name: Osc-B Level
key_parameters.does: Modulation depth. This is the FM 'brightness' control; small changes alter the timbre drastically.

key_parameters.name: Filter Freq
key_parameters.does: Post-FM filter cutoff.

key_parameters.name: Volume Attack / Decay / Sustain / Release
key_parameters.does: Amplitude envelope. Long attack plus long release gives a pad; short both gives a pluck.

devices.gotchas: FM timbre depends on ratios, not absolute pitches, so a patch that works on one note can be unrecognisable two octaves down.

devices.name: Wavetable
devices.summary: Wavetable synthesis. The default choice for evolving pads and modern basses.

key_parameters.name: Osc 1 Position
key_parameters.does: Position in the wavetable. Automating this is what makes a pad evolve rather than sit still.

key_parameters.name: Osc 1 Effect 1 / 2
key_parameters.does: Per-oscillator effect amounts; what they do depends on the effect mode selected.

key_parameters.name: Filter 1 Frequency
key_parameters.does: Cutoff.

key_parameters.name: Filter 1 Resonance
key_parameters.does: Emphasis.

key_parameters.name: Amp Attack / Decay / Sustain / Release
key_parameters.does: Amplitude envelope.

key_parameters.name: Unison Amount
key_parameters.does: Detune spread. Widens a sound, at the cost of pitch definition and mono compatibility.

devices.gotchas: Unison widening makes a part occupy far more stereo and frequency space than its note range implies, the usual reason several pads stop fitting together.

devices.name: Instrument Rack
devices.summary: A container holding several instruments in parallel chains, with eight Macro controls mapped across them.

key_parameters.name: Macro 1-8
key_parameters.does: Whatever the patch's author mapped. On a factory preset these are the intended performance controls, and usually the best things to automate. Their names tell you what they do.

devices.gotchas: Use get_rack_chains to see the layers and their mixer levels. Automating a Macro moves every parameter mapped to it at once, which is usually what you want; reaching a nested device directly needs chain_path.

devices.name: Arpeggiator
devices.summary: Turns held notes into patterns. Placed before an instrument in the chain.

key_parameters.name: Rate
key_parameters.does: Note speed, synced to tempo. 1/16 is the common choice.

key_parameters.name: Style
key_parameters.does: Pattern direction, up, down, up-down, converge, diverge, random and others.

key_parameters.name: Steps
key_parameters.does: How many octaves or transposition steps the pattern climbs.

key_parameters.name: Gate
key_parameters.does: Note length as a proportion of the rate. Below 100% gives separation; above overlaps.

key_parameters.name: Groove
key_parameters.does: Swing feel.

devices.gotchas: The arpeggiator generates notes at playback and they are not written into the clip, so get_clip_notes will not show them.

devices.name: Saturator
devices.summary: Simpler saturation than Roar. Good for warmth and glue without much character change.

key_parameters.name: Drive
key_parameters.does: Amount of saturation.

key_parameters.name: Output
key_parameters.does: Level compensation.

key_parameters.name: Dry/Wet
key_parameters.does: Blend.

key_parameters.name: Type
key_parameters.does: Saturation curve, analog clip, soft sine, digital clip and others.

devices.name: Limiter
devices.summary: Ceiling control. Belongs on the master, last in the chain.

key_parameters.name: Ceiling
key_parameters.does: Maximum output level. -0.3 dB is a safe target.

key_parameters.name: Gain
key_parameters.does: Input drive. Raising this is what makes things louder, and squashes dynamics.

key_parameters.name: Release
key_parameters.does: Recovery speed. Auto is usually right.

devices.gotchas: A limiter fixes peaks, not a mix. If it is working hard, the problem is upstream.

devices.name: Chorus-Ensemble
devices.summary: Modulated widening and thickening. Standard on pads and electric pianos.

key_parameters.name: Amount
key_parameters.does: Modulation depth.

key_parameters.name: Rate
key_parameters.does: Modulation speed. Slow is lush; fast becomes vibrato.

key_parameters.name: Dry/Wet
key_parameters.does: Blend.

key_parameters.name: Mode
key_parameters.does: Classic, Ensemble or Vibrato.

devices.gotchas: Widens the stereo image, so several chorused parts stop being separable. Check mono compatibility.
